narration.short: Surface temperature within 150 m of this address against the city's land average, from clear summer Landsat images.

final.paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**In brief.**
This address is outside the 2012 Sandy inundation footprint [sandy_inundation], in FEMA flood zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard) on the 2007 effective map [fema_nfhl], and outside the modeled flooding in the DEP stormwater scenarios for current, 2050 and 2080 sea-level rise [dep_moderate_current][dep_moderate_2050][dep_extreme_2080]. 89 flood-related 311 complaints were filed within 200 m in the last 5 years [nyc311].

**Hazard Reader.**
This address sits outside the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC Open Data) [sandy_inundation]. This address sits in FEMA flood zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard), per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970234F, effective 2007 [fema_nfhl]. FEMA's preliminary flood map (PFIRM issued 2015-01-30, community 360497) places this address in zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard) [fema_pfirm]. A preliminary map is not the effective map and does not set flood insurance. NYC DEP stormwater scenarios at this address: current sea level with 2.13 in/hr of rain, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_current]; 2050 sea-level rise with 2.13 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_2050]; 2080 sea-level rise with 3.66 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_extreme_2080]. USGS surveyed 2 Hurricane Ida high-water marks within 800 m of this address; the highest stood 0.76 ft above ground; the highest water surface elevation was 48.2 ft NAVD88 [ida_hwm]. Nearest mark: Intersection of 182nd St. and 90th Ave., Jamaica, Queens (174 m away) [ida_hwm]. Elevation 14.87 m; this point is higher than 29% of the ground within 200 m (the 29th percentile; a low percentile means a local low spot where water collects) [microtopo].

**Live Observer.**
2 FloodNet community sensors within 600 m have logged 14 above-curb flood events in the last 3 years, the most recent starting 2026-09-01 05:39 UTC [floodnet]. Peak depth recorded by the sensors in good working order: 815 mm (32.1 in) on 2026-05-20 [floodnet]. 1 sensor that logged 11 of these events is flagged by FloodNet for maintenance, so its depths are not used for the peak [floodnet]. The highest depth a flagged sensor recorded was 1172 mm (46.1 in) on 2026-05-20 [floodnet]. 89 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years: 48 sewer backup, 28 catch basin, 10 street flooding, 3 manhole overflow [nyc311]. Nearest USGS stream gauge, Alley Creek Near Oakland Gardens NY (01302050, 5.7 km away): stage 0.28 ft, observed 2026-10-02 15:00 UTC [usgs_gauges].

**Asset Register.**
16 MTA subway entrances within 800 m of this address; of the nearest 8: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 8 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [mta_entrance_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise), by station: Jamaica-179 St (F) (445 m) [mta_entrance_exposure]. 1 flood-exposed NYCHA development within 2000 m of this address (the register lists only developments found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every development): 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 1 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [nycha_development_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise): CONLON LIHFE TOWER (1048 m) [nycha_development_exposure]. 0 flood-exposed NYC DOE schools within 1500 m of this address (the register lists only schools found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every school): 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doe_school_exposure]. 1 hospital within 3000 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doh_hospital_exposure].

**Projector.**
No active NWS flood, coastal or wind alerts at this point, checked 2026-10-02 15:37 UTC [nws_alerts]. NPCC4 (2024) projects sea-level rise in New York City of 14 to 19 in (0.36 to 0.48 m) by the 2050s and 30 to 50 in (0.76 to 1.27 m) by 2100, relative to 1995-2014, as its middle range (25th to 75th percentile); the 90th percentile is 23 in (0.58 m) by the 2050s and 65 in (1.65 m) by 2100 [npcc4_slr].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.

landcover.narrative: Experimental: a satellite land-cover model estimates that 83.7% of the ground within 500 m of this address is paved or built over and 16.0% is green (9.5% tree canopy), on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2026; no change between years is read from it. Limits: it estimates the share of each 10 m satellite pixel that is canopy, grass, paving, roof, water or bare ground, learned from the city's 2017 six-inch map, so detail finer than about 30 m is blurred and a tree over a street counts as canopy; against the city's own 2021 six-inch map, on squares it never trained on, it read a typical district's paved share 1.7 points above the map's (at most 7.8 points off in the 46 districts with enough test ground) and its mean error per land-cover group was 4.8 points at best, more than the 3.0 points of the city's 2017 map read as if it were 2021, so the 2017 map is the more accurate source for its year; two images of one summer differ by under 2.0 points in a district's paved share 19 times in 20, but between 2018 and 2024 the shares of 49 of 59 districts differ by more, so its maps of different years are not compared. Rely on NYC's own land cover maps (2017 and 2021, 6 inch) and building footprints for a survey.

ttm_battery_surge.narrative: Experimental forecast: the water at The Battery may run up to 0.16 m (0.5 ft) above NOAA's predicted tide in the next 96 hours, counted from 2026-10-02 15:00 UTC, most around 2026-10-05 16:00 UTC; added to the predicted tide, the highest total would be 5.7 ft above MLLW on 2026-10-02 17:00 UTC, below the gauge's minor flood stage of 7.0 ft. Limits: it reads only the last 1,024 hours of the Battery gauge, with no wind or pressure input, so it cannot see a storm that has not yet reached the gauge; on 635 past 96-hour windows (2025-01-01 to 2026-09-27) its mean error was 11.5 cm, against 13.3 cm for assuming the last day's mean continues, and it foresaw 1 of the 23 windows in which the water reached the minor flood stage. Rely on the National Weather Service (weather.gov/okx) and Notify NYC; NOAA's ETSS and the Stevens Flood Advisory System model surge from the weather.

npcc4_slr.narrative: NPCC4 (2024) projects sea-level rise in New York City of 14 to 19 in (0.36 to 0.48 m) by the 2050s and 30 to 50 in (0.76 to 1.27 m) by 2100, relative to 1995-2014, as its middle range (25th to 75th percentile); the 90th percentile is 23 in (0.58 m) by the 2050s and 65 in (1.65 m) by 2100.
